prompt:
Classic hand-drawn Japanese animated feature-film food illustration, in the warm, gentle Miyazaki-inspired style of this website. Precise thin warm-brown outlines, clean cel colours, restrained two-tone shading, softly lit cream and muted turquoise kitchen palette. Detailed culinary technique, natural believable objects. Absolutely no photorealism, lens effects, grain, paper texture, painterly speckles, fractal or Mandelbrot detail. A single clear scene, never a diagram, collage, contact sheet, arrows or labels.

Rules: smooth, clean surfaces with crisp, well-defined outlines — no grain, noise, hatching, stippling, paper or crackle texture anywhere. Draw only what the scene names; nothing carried over from other steps. Food is in exactly the state the scene describes — nothing cooked, assembled or garnished ahead of time. Cooked egg is silky and glossy in soft folds, never curdled, foamy or pebbly; simmering liquid is smooth with only a few clean bubbles; rice is a soft mound with a modest number of clearly drawn grains. Cuts, sizes and quantities exactly as described and realistic. When a hand steadies food during knife work, it uses a proper claw grip (guiding fingertips tucked under, knuckles against the blade). A chicken thigh fillet is small and thin — about palm-sized (12 × 8 cm), 1–2 cm thick, irregular, pale pink with a little white fat — never a big thick slab, never marbled red like pork or beef. Hands belong to one right-handed cook seen from their own position: the right hand does the knife/chopsticks/pouring work from the right side of the frame, the left hand steadies or holds the pan handle from the left; keep the camera angle the same across a recipe's pictures. Prefer a tight close-up where the subject fills the frame.

Keep the exact same soft golden SCRAMBLED EGG FOLDS mixed through thick red tomato sauce and small green pepper dice. Add only SIX small irregular WHITE CHEESE CRUMBLES, each 1 cm, on top. Do not replace folded eggs with whole eggs: NO fried egg circles, NO egg-white discs, NO intact yolks, NO poached eggs. No onions or fresh herb garnish. Set the pan on the cream counter with a little bread beside it. Clean warm Japanese hand-drawn animation style, flat cel food, no microtexture.

Render EVERYTHING, especially food, as clean hand-drawn animation cels: two or three broad flat colour regions per ingredient, sparse readable contours, and broad soft shadows. Food must never look like a photograph pasted into an illustrated kitchen. No pores, micro-speckles, fine fibres, tiny scale meshes, stippled highlights or photographic surface texture. Describe tenderness and crispness with a few large shapes and folds, not tiny marks.

How to draw small repeated things (rice grains, bubbles, crumbs, starch, flour, panko, crust nubs, sesame seeds, salt, sugar, chilli and spice flakes, bonito flakes, nori bits): draw each one INDIVIDUALLY as a distinct, separate piece — a simple clean shape with its own thin crisp outline, smooth cel shading and one small highlight, all at the same readable size (each at least about 1/80 of the picture width), like individually placed game sprites. Show a countable number — a few dozen, not hundreds. Never a dense swarm or speckled field, never clusters made of smaller clusters, never pieces shrinking into ever-tinier copies toward the edges: no fractal, self-similar, recursive, frothy, foamy, beaded, sponge-like or cauliflower-like surfaces. Where there would really be hundreds, draw the mass as one smooth flat-coloured shape and outline only a few dozen individual pieces on its surface and edges. Leave visible space between pieces — never a carpet of overlapping detailed pieces filling the frame. Small creatures (baby fish, tiny shrimp) are simplified to a clean silhouette with one eye dot — no scales, stripes or segments. Hot oil and simmering liquid: a smooth glossy surface with a dozen or so separate round bubbles, no froth. Fried crust is NOT made of pieces: a smooth, glossy, crisp shell following the food's softly lumpy shape, with a few soft creases and ridges and a handful of small flakes at its edges — never beads, dots, nubs, popcorn or cauliflower texture.
